vibe.rationale: Vibe 5 — one-session hold from June 24 evening's Vibe 5. The hold reflects a session where one axis delivered a genuine milestone while the primary normalization gating conditions remained unchanged. The positive: Kartar Fire jumped from 40% to 80% containment in 24 hours, driven by the Thursday night showers that delivered on schedule — the most rapid single-day containment improvement of the fire period and the most significant PNW operational win since the acute June 22-23 escalation. All evacuations are downgraded or lifted; aerial resources have halted; personnel reduced to 210. The fire is tracking toward full containment ahead of the East Cascades onset window (T-3, approximately June 29). This materially reduces the compounding-resource-demand risk that has defined the PNW axis since June 22. Lebanon ceasefire has cleared the 72-hour stability threshold and is approaching the 96-hour mark — further consolidating the clearance of the first of three Vibe 7 conditions. Wall Street is rebounding from the June 23 semiconductor selloff, which removes the acute equity-market negative that characterized the June 24 evening. The reasons this does not upgrade to Vibe 6: (1) Iran's formal Hormuz re-closure retraction has not been issued. Day 7 of contested compliance with the parliament ratification window closed June 25 but no publicly confirmed outcome. Ratification is the procedural upstream condition for a downstream IRGC- or executive-level position change — that downstream action has not been announced. Lloyd's war-risk normalization remains blocked. The 118-tanker backlog and Kpler's normalization trajectory remain gated on Iran's formal move. (2) Nuclear inspection dispute between the US and Iran over IAEA access to bombed nuclear sites has not resolved — this is the most credible complication for Switzerland Round 2 framing and the 60-day MOU timeline. (3) SCOTUS June 25 anticipated opinion day introduced acute domestic uncertainty — Trump v. Barbara (birthright citizenship) and Watson v. RNC (mail ballot counting) possibly dropped today; no confirmed rulings through the evening brief window, but the combined legal concentration with Louisiana v. Callais operative creates the brief cycle's highest domestic legal risk density. Vibe 4 trigger conditions: Lebanon ceasefire formal collapse with resumed Hezbollah-IDF escalation; Iran IRGC active physical interdiction of Hormuz transit (absent through Day 7); SCOTUS birthright citizenship ruling with broad immediate enforcement mechanism triggering mass-litigation wave.

items.summary: The June 25 evening geopolitical picture is defined by three interlocking elements: the Lebanon ceasefire consolidating past the 72-hour threshold toward the 96-hour mark, Iran's parliament completing its MOU ratification vote window without a publicly confirmed outcome, and Iran's formal Hormuz re-closure declaration remaining operative for a seventh consecutive compliance day. The Lebanon ceasefire has held approximately 76 hours without a formal void declaration from either Israel or Hezbollah. Tactical violations continue on both sides — IDF infrastructure strikes in Lebanon persist; Hezbollah maintains rocket and anti-tank response against Israeli military positions — but the operative distinction between tactical violations and declared ceasefire collapse has held through the 72-hour threshold. The 96-hour mark (~20 hours out from the evening brief) is the next durability milestone. Netanyahu's withdrawal timeline announcement was identified in the June 24 watch list as the ceasefire's most consequential structural test: a credible phased-withdrawal commitment provides the political scaffolding for Iran's re-closure retraction to be domestically defensible. No confirmed Netanyahu announcement was available through the evening brief window. On Iran's parliament: the Majlis ratification vote was expected to conclude by June 25. Ratification is the procedural mechanism formally authorizing the Iranian executive and IRGC to comply with the MOU, including modifying the Hormuz re-closure declaration. A parliamentary rejection or conditional approval would materially complicate the MOU's 60-day framework. No confirmed outcome was available as of the evening brief. On the re-closure's operational character: market intelligence from Windward AI and Kpler AIS data continues to confirm that Iran's June 20-21 re-closure declaration functions as symbolic leverage rather than a physically enforced closure — 25 AIS-visible transits were recorded June 22, including French- and Qatari-linked LNG carriers, against CENTCOM's ongoing operational transit confirmation. The contested-but-open frame holds through Compliance Day 7. Lloyd's war-risk normalization remains the commercial gate: insurance premiums have not normalized; the 118-tanker backlog cannot be released commercially without Lloyd's announcement, which is gated on Iran's formal position change. WTI is trading approximately $73.7 — a third consecutive day below the $74 normalization-confidence floor, confirming sustained market repricing of normalization probability. The Swiss technical talks Round 2 framework remains complicated by the nuclear inspection dispute (IAEA access to bombed sites, contested between the US and Iran) and the Iranian challenge to the unfrozen asset control framework. Pakistan continues mediating. The US Treasury's 60-day suspension of Iranian oil sanctions remains active, and Gulf producers (Kuwait, ADNOC) continue lifting output.

items.summary: The June 25 evening economic picture reflects a market rebound from the June 23 semiconductor-driven selloff, with forward attention concentrating on two imminent data catalysts: May PCE inflation data (expected Friday June 27 at 08:30 ET) and Micron earnings. Wall Street is rebounding intraday on June 25, reversing a portion of the -1.44% S&P 500 and -2.21% Nasdaq losses from June 23. The Schwab session framing — 'Wall Street Rebounds Awaiting Micron, PCE Prices' — captures the dual-driver character: memory chip names stabilizing after South Korean market losses, and PCE data anticipated as the week's most consequential Fed-policy data point. Wells Fargo economists project May PCE up 0.5% month-over-month, which would push the annual PCE rate to 4.1% — meaningfully above the Federal Reserve's 2% target and consistent with the hawkish tone of Chair Warsh's June 17 FOMC press conference. An above-forecast PCE print would confirm energy-cost passthrough from the Hormuz closure into consumption prices with a lag, providing empirical support for the nine FOMC members who projected at least one 2026 rate hike in the June Summary of Economic Projections. A below-forecast print would reduce the immediate hawkish pressure and support the current Warsh hold framing. The July 27 PCE data will set the trading frame heading into the July 4 holiday weekend. The European Central Bank and Bank of Japan are also in a tightening posture for June, with June hikes followed by further moves in Scandinavia and New Zealand expected next quarter — creating a synchronized global tightening backdrop that constrains the Fed's ability to hold if US PCE runs hot. WTI holds approximately $73.7 for a third consecutive session below the $74 normalization-confidence floor. This confirms sustained market repricing of normalization probability rather than a single-session anomaly. However, pump relief for consumers requires Lloyd's normalization, not WTI pricing alone. The downstream chain — Iran retraction → Lloyd's announcement → 118-tanker backlog release → WTI $65-70 supply pulse → pump relief — remains gated on Iran's formal move. Oregon pump price at approximately $5.35/gallon; national at approximately $4.56/gallon. The Federal Reserve macro framework is unchanged: Warsh hold at 3.50-3.75%, nine of 19 FOMC members projecting at least one 2026 hike, PCE SEP projection at 3.6%, GDP 2.2%. Bank Indonesia raised its key rate 25 basis points to 5.75% at its June meeting — third increase in roughly a month — reflecting the global inflation-fighting context.

items.summary: The June 25 evening infrastructure picture is dominated by the Kartar Fire's jump to 80% containment — the most significant single-session operational improvement of the PNW fire period. The Thursday night showers (June 25) delivered on schedule as NWS Seattle and Portland had forecast since early in the week. The combined effect of the Gulf of Alaska system's cooling and delivered precipitation has materially improved fire behavior conditions across eastern Washington. At 80% containment and approximately 11,746 acres, the fire has secured roughly 9,400 acres inside defensible perimeter lines — a 40-percentage-point jump from 40% in the June 24 evening brief. All evacuation notices in the Kartar Valley, Columbia River Road, Kartar Road, and Omak Lake Road zones have been downgraded or lifted, enabling displaced residents to return to assessed areas. Aerial resources have halted water and retardant drops — the standard milestone transition indicating that fire behavior has been suppressed to the point where air support is no longer operationally required. Personnel have decreased from 260 to 210, consistent with the transition from active suppression to ground consolidation. The incident management team (Type 3 Northeast Washington Interagency) continues direct attack and perimeter-bolstering operations. The remaining approximately 20% uncontained perimeter requires continued ground work before lines can be declared complete. The operational significance for the East Cascades onset window (T-3, approximately June 29): the principal risk identified in prior briefs — that an active, under-contained Kartar Fire combined with new East Cascades onset ignitions would exceed NIFC PL3 resource allocation capacity — is now materially reduced. The fire is tracking toward full containment ahead of the onset window. This does not eliminate onset-window ignition risk for new fires across the east Cascades and Columbia Basin, but it removes the compounding factor that defined the June 22-24 risk calculation. BPA grid is stable on Day 5 post-heat-advisory with no forced outages. NIFC PL3 Day 8. Oregon EO 26-10 Day 11 at 414 fires and 8,000+ acres YTD.

items.summary: The June 25 evening domestic landscape is dominated by acute SCOTUS concentration — Thursday June 25 is an anticipated opinion day for the remaining term-end cases, with Trump v. Barbara (birthright citizenship, EO 14160) and Watson v. RNC (mail ballot counting) potentially issuing at any point during Thursday sessions or the remaining term days. No confirmed rulings were available as of the evening brief window, but the Court's end-of-June-term pattern typically produces consecutive opinion days in the final week, and both cases have been outstanding since April oral argument. The combined legal concentration — Louisiana v. Callais operative since June 23, Trump v. Barbara and Watson v. RNC outstanding — represents the highest domestic legal risk density of the brief cycle. Trump v. Barbara tests EO 14160 (signed January 20, 2025), which would deny automatic birthright citizenship to US-born children unless at least one parent holds US citizenship or LPR status. Every lower court has found EO 14160 violates the 14th Amendment citizenship clause. Oral argument questioning (April 1, 2026) was described as 'icy' toward the government's position. The 6-3 conservative supermajority creates irreducible outcome uncertainty despite the lower-court consensus. Watson v. RNC determines whether states can count ballots postmarked by Election Day but received after — the operational mechanics of mail-ballot counting for November 2026 midterms. Whichever way Watson lands, it reshapes state election administration planning with less than five months to November. Louisiana v. Callais (issued June 23, 6-3) remains operative: the Alabama discriminatory congressional map is being applied to 2026 elections per the SCOTUS order, the Section 2 VRA evidentiary bar has been substantially raised, and Senate Democrats under Schumer are exploring a new VRA legislative pathway with uncertain prospects in the 119th Congress. New York House balance district primaries (NY-3, NY-4, NY-12, NY-17, NY-19) have finalized through the June 24-25 tabulation window. Reconciliation 2.0: T-4 to the Rules Committee June 30 deadline; Thursday has passed without a scheduling announcement, making Friday June 26 the final practical pre-deadline date. Trump administration has received court authorization to resume nationwide expedited deportation operations following a Tuesday federal appeals court ruling, operationalizing a further element of Secure America Act implementation.

items.headline: Kartar Fire 80% Containment MILESTONE — Thursday Showers Delivered; All Evacuations Downgraded or Lifted; Aerial Resources Halted; Personnel 260→210; East Cascades Onset T-3 (~June 29); Compounding Risk MATERIALLY REDUCED; BPA Stable Day 5; Oregon EO 26-10 Day 11; Six WA Fires Progressing
items.summary: The June 25 evening PNW picture is shaped by the Kartar Fire's milestone containment jump — the brief cycle's most significant single-session PNW operational development. Thursday night showers delivered as forecast, and the fire's response has exceeded expectations: 40 percentage points of containment gained in 24 hours represents the most rapid single-day improvement since the fire's ignition on June 16. All evacuation notices in the Kartar Valley zone have been downgraded or lifted, with many previously closed roads now reopened. Aerial resources have halted water and retardant drops — the transition signal indicating fire behavior has been suppressed to the point where ground operations are primary. Ground crews (210 personnel, down from 260) are consolidating perimeter lines toward full containment declaration. The operational significance for the East Cascades onset window (T-3, approximately June 29): the compounding-resource-demand risk that has defined the PNW axis since June 22 — an active, under-contained Kartar Fire meeting new East Cascades onset ignitions — is now materially reduced. The fire is tracking toward full containment ahead of the onset window. This does not eliminate onset-window ignition risk for new fires across the broader east Cascades and Columbia Basin, but it removes the compounding factor. BPA grid is stable on Day 5 post-heat-advisory with no forced outages and temperatures near seasonal normal. NIFC PL3 Day 8. Oregon EO 26-10 Day 11 at 414 fires and 8,000+ acres YTD. Six concurrent large fires in Washington continue progressing toward resolution: Tule Road at approximately 95%, Juniper Dunes at approximately 90%, Upriver in mop-up. Oregon coast has seen its 21st gray whale washup in 2026 near Lincoln City — a continuing signal of marine ecosystem stress that has tracked throughout the brief cycle. Six orca sightings have been reported along the Oregon coast this period.

items.summary: Secondary PNW environmental and regional threads on June 25 evening. NSF Newport OR ocean observatory now T-2 days from the monitoring gap opening (~June 28). The practical window for an emergency bridge monitoring arrangement has narrowed to Friday June 26 as the last possible business day for a federal emergency coordination decision. Two days is not sufficient for normal procurement pathways. The gap will open during the East Cascades onset window (T-3, approximately June 29-July 1), removing the coastal atmospheric anchor for fire-weather modeling at the onset period's most consequential moment. The Kartar Fire's 80% containment milestone slightly reduces the net risk profile — fewer simultaneous active suppression operations will require coastal-atmospheric-anchored fire-weather modeling when the gap opens — but new onset-window ignitions will still lack the Newport station's data feed. Super El Niño watch continues at 25% probability (KLCC/OPB June 22). The strong El Niño base probability is 61%; the 'very strong' designation carries a 25% overlay per NOAA. No new ENSO consensus shift since the KLCC report; next formal update expected early July. A Super El Niño in 2026-2027 would produce a critically dry, warm fifth consecutive PNW drought winter — 2027 fire conditions structurally exceeding the elevated 2026 baseline. Thursday's showers provide fine-fuel moisture benefit for active suppression but carry no drought-meaningful precipitation quantity; aquifer and snowpack recharge pathways remain closed until fall. Washington drought emergency advances to Day 22 — fourth consecutive year, 12 emergency counties, 50% statewide snowpack vs. normal. Oregon drought affects approximately 83% of the state, including 17 counties under emergency order. L-Pod orca calf is entering its fourth week alive — a continued positive for the critically endangered Southern Resident Killer Whale population whose reproductive success has been near zero for multiple years. The 21st Oregon gray whale washup is the marine mammal stress backdrop for a broader marine ecosystem concern across the Pacific Northwest coast. Echinococcus multilocularis peri-urban surveillance in Washington State coyote populations continues active with no new confirmed spread events. Amazon Washington State WARN (2,198 positions) continues as the structural PNW tech-labor bifurcation backdrop.

analyst_summary: June 25, 2026 evening closes at Vibe 5 — one-session hold from the June 24 evening Vibe 5 position, and the brief cycle's fourth consecutive Vibe 5 session. The session's operational headline is the Kartar Fire's jump to 80% containment following the delivery of Thursday night's showers — a 40-percentage-point improvement in 24 hours that is the most significant single-session PNW operational development of the June fire period. All evacuations in the Kartar Valley are downgraded or lifted; aerial resources have halted; personnel reduced to 210. The fire is tracking toward full containment ahead of the East Cascades onset window (T-3, approximately June 29). The compounding-resource-demand risk that has defined the PNW axis since the June 22 acute escalation is now materially reduced. Against this genuine win, the geopolitical normalization chain's core missing link remains unchanged on Day 7 of contested compliance: Iran's formal Hormuz re-closure retraction has still not been issued. The parliament ratification vote window closed June 25 without a publicly confirmed outcome — passage would have been the upstream procedural mechanism for a downstream executive- or IRGC-level re-closure modification, which is the Lloyd's normalization gate. Lloyd's remains blocked. The 118-tanker backlog remains stranded. The nuclear inspection dispute between the US and Iran over IAEA access to bombed nuclear sites continues to complicate Switzerland Round 2 framing. Lebanon ceasefire has cleared the 72-hour threshold and is approaching the 96-hour mark without a formal void declaration — directionally positive but not the downstream action that triggers normalization. WTI holds below $74 for a third consecutive day, confirming sustained market pricing of normalization probability, while Wall Street rebounds from the June 23 selloff ahead of PCE data on June 27 (Wells Fargo projects +0.5% MoM, 4.1% annual — a hawkish upside scenario). Domestically, June 25 was an anticipated SCOTUS opinion day for Trump v. Barbara and Watson v. RNC — no confirmed rulings through the evening brief, but both cases remain outstanding as the term approaches its close, creating the brief cycle's highest domestic legal concentration alongside the operative Louisiana v. Callais. Reconciliation 2.0 Thursday window slipped; Friday June 26 is the final practical pre-deadline scheduling window before the June 30 Rules Committee deadline. NSF Newport OR advances to T-2 before the monitoring gap opens (~June 28) — with no bridge arrangement announced, the coastal atmospheric anchor for fire-weather modeling will be lost during the East Cascades onset window.
